## Functional identification

The sequence is an **arylsulfatase** (UniProt **P28607**) from *Pseudoalteromonas carrageenovora*. This assignment is highly reliable because the query sequence is an **exact 100% sequence match** to the reviewed reference protein.

The N-terminal 25 residues are a signal peptide, consistent with export to the **periplasm**, where the enzyme can act on sulfated polysaccharides.

## Catalytic reaction

The enzyme catalyzes hydrolysis of an aryl sulfate ester:

\[
\text{aryl sulfate} + \mathrm{H_2O}
\rightarrow
\text{phenol} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}} + \mathrm{H^+}
\]

More generally:

\[
\mathrm{Ar{-}O{-}SO_3^- + H_2O \rightarrow Ar{-}OH + SO_4^{2-} + H^+}
\]

This corresponds to **EC 3.1.6.1**, arylsulfatase activity, and **Rhea RHEA:17261**.

## Summary

This is a secreted/periplasmic **arylsulfatase (glycosulphohydrolase)** that removes sulfate groups from sulfated aromatic or polysaccharide-associated substrates, yielding the desulfated phenolic product and inorganic sulfate. The sequence contains Lactamase B-related domain signatures, consistent with this enzyme family.
